Header.CaseTitle: Crossfield Trading Ltd v Northern Commercial Bank Plc

Counsel.Lead: Michael Moore KC; Victoria Clarke (instructed by Allen & Overy LLP)

SummaryOfPosition.Summary: The Appellant claims damages for breach of contract and negligent mis-statement arising from the Respondent's sale of interest rate hedging products that were unsuitable for the Appellant's needs and sophistication level.

FactsReliedOn.item: The Appellant is a small trading company with turnover of approximately £3 million annually.
In 2015, the Respondent sold the Appellant a structured collar interest rate swap with a 10-year term.
The Appellant was classified as a retail client but was not given appropriate protections.
The product resulted in break costs of £890,000 when the Appellant sought to refinance in 2019.
The Appellant was not informed of the potential magnitude of break costs.

Contentions.item: The Respondent breached COBS rules by failing to ensure the product was suitable.
The Respondent misrepresented the nature and risks of the product.
The Appellant was wrongly classified as a professional client.
The break costs were a concealed and unfair term.

LegalBasis.item: Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Regulated Activities) Order 2001
